title: Upstream reconstruction and runtime maintenance
summary: Review nine material upstream changes across reconstruction fidelity, original retro tooling, playable ports, disk-image preservation and repository lineage.
notes: The CPU audit queue contained zero unresolved source/target CPU areas. This pass nevertheless resolved two newly evidenced output decisions: The Puzzle Pits publishes x86-64 builds, and Amberstar.net publishes Windows/Linux x64 assets. No minimum hardware profile was inferred from those output architectures. Primary commits, pinned documentation and the Amberstar prerelease were reviewed; the tracker did not compile or execute upstream projects.

sources.reason: Canonical home of the migrated Amberstar reimplementation, legacy data loaders, scenario tests and native AOT releases; the shared Amber engine is consumed as packages.

source_updates.reason: Reviewed the new finite launch-state contracts and exact generated-output accounting; no separate target or minimum hardware profile appeared.
Reviewed the recovered maze-sound C routine and updated 271/1,099 C-coverage statement; retained the staged reconstruction boundary.
Reviewed the headless CyborgOS platform, generated-output regression and pause/state service additions as one original compiler project.
Reviewed the DOS throw/global-unwind bank and its explicit zero-new-exact-byte, EFLAGS and whole-TU limits.
Reviewed the shared IVM generator/printer refactor and preserved OrWin's original-homebrew classification.
Reviewed symbol-driven CPU-identity disk editing, safe image replacement flow and focused checks; no nested project was created.
Reviewed the standard-varargs cleanup and full-executable exactness evidence while retaining remaining compiler-input blockers.
Reviewed current playable release/build documentation, x64 output evidence, editor relationship and differential gameplay-rule correction.
Reviewed the explicit migration of Amberstar game projects to Amberstar.net; the shared Amber repository remains an engine dependency rather than the canonical game root.

project.status: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes while common airborne and ground launch-state contracts reduce unresolved record accesses from 219 to 207; broader semantics and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.

identity.narrative: M68k Reversing Toolkit remains the same generated Amiga analysis and reconstruction framework; the reviewed change advances its Starglider 2 restoration rather than creating a separate project.

classification.narrative: The change is bounded reconstruction/tooling work: canonical ancestry is used to retain a safe common custom pointer prefix without treating that prefix as proof of equal values, subtype, lifetime or complete semantics.

source_cpu.narrative: The tracked Starglider 2 input remains Motorola 68000 code; no new architecture is inferred from the analysis implementation.

target_cpu.narrative: The retained output is native Motorola 68000 assembly, verified upstream against the original binary through the existing C/vasm route.

build.narrative: The reviewed launch-state pass recovers 12 typed accesses across finite airborne and ground spawn tables, raising typed accesses to 2,589 and reducing unresolved record accesses to 207 while retaining the existing exact 412,736-byte output.
build.limitations: These are upstream generated-output and targeted semantic checks. The tracker did not run the generator or game, and BYTE 41 parameters, ground BYTE 43 writes and 264 ownership intervals remain unresolved.
build.next_action: Continue classifying unresolved accesses and ownership intervals without promoting bounded exact generation to complete behavioral reconstruction.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed restoration evidence does not state a minimum Amiga CPU, RAM, chipset or ROM configuration.
runtime_profiles.next_action: Add a runtime profile only when primary documentation or qualified hardware/emulator testing states a concrete minimum configuration.

ai.narrative: Existing explicit Claude contribution evidence remains valid; the reviewed commit does not add a new attribution category.

relationships.narrative: The current restoration remains within the Starglider 2 target and does not resolve the wider predecessor, successor or credited-source graph.
relationships.next_action: Revisit project relationships after the bounded restoration stabilizes.

project.status: MAINL gains source-present DOS exception throw and global-unwind recovery covering 2,524 original bank bytes, but adds zero exact bytes; candidate size, EFLAGS and whole-TU gaps remain explicit.

identity.narrative: Scoped source recovery of MAIN, OP, MAINL and ZUN artifacts. README separates exact owned functions from source-present work and says whole-game reconstruction remains unfinished. The new candidates remain within the same scoped MAIN/OP/MAINL/ZUN recovery; neither controlled layout experiments nor candidate bodies expand the exact-function ledger.

classification.narrative: Scope: source-reconstruction / game. Primary README, repository file layout and selected implementation files were reviewed.

target_cpu.narrative: Target architecture x86. Host ports and minimum variants are not inferred from source CPU.

build.narrative: The review resolves 2,446 instruction bytes plus 78 compiler-generated exception-handling bytes across eight far procedures, with native BCC 4.5/TASM/TLINK rounds and focused 386 context/unwind probes. Accepted MAINL ownership remains 211 extents, 288 procedures and 36,946 bytes, so this adds source presence but zero new exact bytes.
build.limitations: The candidate bank remains raw-different, the saved EFLAGS probe differs (0x80 versus original 0x84), the 16-bit resume branch and complete throw/catch lifecycle were not executed, and this is not a complete translation unit or whole-game result.
build.next_action: Recover the remaining front jump/name and tail RTTI functions, integrate the full translation unit, and resolve the code-generation, frame and storage gaps.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The new scoped acceptance material adds no verified minimum PC-98 CPU, RAM or peripheral requirement.

ai.narrative: Project-scoped agent instructions/configuration provide an AI-use signal; the particular agent is not inferred.

relationships.narrative: Checked current catalogue, source and decision URLs and related titles. Scoped source recovery of MAIN, OP, MAINL and ZUN artifacts. README separates exact owned functions from source-present work and says whole-game reconstruction remains unfinished.

project.status: ND100X adds a disk-image CPU-identity editor that resolves SINTRAN symbols and segment pages from the mounted pack, ejects before patching, verifies the stored image and remounts it; upstream reports 37 focused checks.

identity.narrative: ND-100/CX full-system emulator with memory-management, storage/network peripherals, BPUN loading, disassembly and DAP debugging, maintained as a substantial nd100em continuation.

classification.narrative: Independent substantial extension: rewritten I/O and memory management, multiple frontends and debugger; author compatibility/boot claims are not independent verification. CPU and debugger headers identify GPL-2.0-or-later and README agrees; root LICENSE contains GPL-3.0 text. Preserve this mixed licensing evidence instead of claiming a clean project-wide resolution. Historical media rights are separate.
